Article Title: Hyderabad family books direct flights to Thailand for Rs 1.16 lakh, airline shifts them to connecting flights with 11-hour layover; Telangana consumer commission orders airline to pay Rs 70,000 compen
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





HYDERABAD: A family from Hyderabad has been awarded Rs 70,000 by a Telangana consumer commission after an airline cancelled their direct flights to Thailand and shifted them to connecting flights, leaving them with stopovers of up to 11 hours. The commission held the airline responsible for deficiency in service, observing that it had failed to establish any valid reason for scrapping the original flight schedule. While the family eventually made the trip on the revised flights, the commission found that the passengers had been left to bear the inconvenience and expenses arising from the changes.The complainant had spent Rs 1,16,477 on round-trip tickets for four passengers travelling between Hyderabad and Phuket from June 6 to 13, 2026. Another Rs 2,949 was paid for additional baggage allowance. Having booked non-stop flights, the family had also made advance reservations at a hotel in Phuket, which were non-refundable. The travel plans changed on May 21, when the airline informed the passengers that their booked flights would no longer operate. Instead of the direct onward flight, the family was assigned a journey with a two-hour-and-40-minute stopover in Bengaluru.The revised return itinerary involved an even longer halt of around 11 hours in the city.The complainant told the commission that the sudden changes caused considerable mental distress to the family and disrupted their holiday plans. He also alleged that the airline made no arrangements for accommodation or other assistance during the extended stopover, leaving him to pay for it himself.The airline's counsel appeared before the commission, but the company did not submit its written version within the prescribed 45-day period. The commission therefore closed its right to file a response. Examining the case, the commission found that the airline had referred to winter schedule changes and operational reasons but had not substantiated why the confirmed flights had to be cancelled and rescheduled. It also pointed out that airlines have a responsibility to provide necessary assistance to passengers when flights are delayed, diverted or cancelled for valid reasons.The commission specifically took note of the family's expenditure during the 11-hour stopover in Bengaluru, observing that the airline had failed to arrange the necessary facilities. Since the passengers had eventually undertaken the journey using the revised flights, the commission considered compensation appropriate rather than treating the entire travel as a failed service. It directed the airline to pay Rs 60,000, working out to Rs 15,000 for each of the four passengers, besides Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. The total compensation awarded was Rs 70,000.
Article Summary: A family from Hyderabad has been awarded Rs 70,000 by a Telangana consumer commission. The airline cancelled their direct flights to Thailand and shifted them to connecting flights, leaving them with stopovers of up to 11 hours. While the family eventually made the trip on the revised flights, the commission found that the passengers had been left to bear the inconvenience and expenses.

Article Title: Days after Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologized for disruption in Outlook services globally, company declares 'Code Red' for its engineers; internal memo says ...
Article Text:
Nadella said the incident was triggered by a previously undetected software bug that surfaced under a specific pattern of user traffic.

‘Most customer-impacting incident’ in Exchange Online history

Engineers battled ‘fog of war’ during outage

Microsoft targets one-hour global recovery

Internal review exposes broader operational weaknesses

Satya Nadella on Microsoft outage

Days after Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologised for a major outage that disrupted Outlook and other Microsoft 265 services across the world, the company has declared ‘Code Red’ initiative which is aimed at overhauling its engineering, incident response and service recovery processes, as per the internal memos reviewed by Reuters. This move from Microsoft comes after the November 12-13 outage which impacted governments, businesses and consumers across multiple countries, including Australia, Japan and the United States. The service disruption affected Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services, raising fresh concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure. Microsoft also said that the incident was not caused by cyberattack or AI-related activity. Instead, the company attributed the outrage to an undetected Windows scalability defect which was introduced un July.According to an internal memo cited by Reuters, M365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as the most customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online. "Never before had so many customers been without email for so long," Henderson reportedly told employees, emphasising that the Code Red designation represents the highest-priority work across the team.The outage lasted nearly 24 hours and affected several core Microsoft cloud services, disrupting communications for enterprises, government agencies and other organisations that rely on Microsoft 365.In a separate memo on Monday, Amanda Silver, a corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, said engineers worked through a “fog of war.” Despite deploying top engineers, responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats and struggled to keep a clear picture of hypotheses and decisions, because diagnostic data was scattered across fragmented internal tracking systems.Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures, according to Silver’s memo.As part of the Code Red effort, Microsoft has launched several high-priority workstreams focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery mechanisms.The company has reportedly set an ambitious goal of resolving future global incidents within one hour. Microsoft also plans to use AI agents to help engineers analyse system health data and diagnose issues more quickly during outages.Henderson is expected to conduct daily reviews with the leadership team overseeing Substrate, the engineering platform that underpins many Microsoft 365 services, alongside weekly progress assessments.Reuters reported that Henderson's review of the outage identified wider organisational and structural issues beyond the specific software defect that triggered the failure. In a separate memo reviewed by the news agency, Henderson said urgent patches for Microsoft 365 Core services were being deployed too slowly across global infrastructure.He reportedly cited a separate recent incident in which a critical production fix required five to six days to achieve worldwide deployment. According to the memo, Microsoft aims to reduce the time between detecting urgent security issues and safely deploying fixes globally to just one hour. "Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday," Henderson wrote, according to Reuters.Microsoft should have caught the software bug that took Outlook offline last week and had safeguards to contain the disruption, chief executive Satya Nadella has said. In an interview with CNBC’s Jim Cramer, Nadella said that the flaw surfaced only under a particular pattern of traffic. “Of course, we should have done the testing before,” he said. The outage disrupted email at businesses that rely on Outlook for day-to-day communication. Nadella said Microsoft should have designed its systems so that a failure in one part of the service could be isolated before it spread globally.He also raised a broader problem for companies running older infrastructure. AI tools can help engineers identify software flaws and develop fixes faster, but each fix still has to be tested and installed. More frequent updates, he said, can make existing systems less stable. His comments pointed to a trade-off for software providers as they accelerate the release of patches while keeping widely used services online."Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable," Nadella said. "I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet."
Article Summary: Microsoft has declared ‘Code Red’ initiative aimed at overhauling its engineering, incident response and service recovery processes. The move comes after the November 12-13 outage which impacted governments, businesses and consumers across multiple countries, including Australia, Japan and the United States. The outage affected Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services.

Article Title: In 1982, Seiko put a Seiko TV in a watch with a 1.2-inch screen, but watching it meant carrying a separate receiver in your pocket
Article Text:
Worn like a digital watch, the TV watch came with a pocket receiver to pick up TV and FM signals (representative image). Image Credits: ChatGPT

A tiny screen packed with new technology

Seiko's LCD TV watch, launched in 1982, had a 1.2-inch screen, but a cable ran up the sleeve to a separate receiver carried in a pocket. Image Credits: @theseikomuseumginza/Instagram

Why the pocket was important

A record breaker that did not catch on

Why the idea still matters

Sneaking a look at a screen in a boring meeting might feel like a modern habit, but in 1982, Seiko tried to do just that with a TV on the wrist. The Seiko Museum Ginza describes the 1982 LCD TV watch as the world's first watch with a tuner and a headphone jack, made for watching TV anywhere, anytime. It had a 1.2-inch screen and was worn on the wrist like a digital watch. However, there was a catch: the wearer had to carry a separate receiver in a pocket to watch anything.The TV screen was 1.2 inches large and had a liquid crystal display, which was a pretty big deal for its time. The museum says it had an advanced LSI chip and liquid crystal technology that was instantly responsive to low voltage. This means that the screen could display moving pictures while requiring very little energy. The watch could still perform basic tasks like the alarm, chronograph, calendar and also tune in to FM radio. Seiko Epson's company history adds that the display was built from a panel first created for watches but modified to display moving images. At the time, the manufacturing company was Suwa Seikosha, and the TV watch was launched under the Seiko brand in December 1982, after being announced earlier that year.The screen on the wrist was only half the story. The Smithsonian Institution's Smithsonian Insider explains that the TV watch needed a receiver and battery pack, both carried in a separate bag or pocket. A cable ran through the sleeve of a jacket and connected the receiver to the wrist screen. The same cable also served as the TV aerial. A headpiece was also needed for the sound, so this tiny TV was really a small kit, not just a watch. Seiko Epson says the TV consumed less power than any before it and could run up to five hours on two AA batteries.Although the gadget was heavier thanks to all the additional equipment, the TV watch was still very well received. Seiko Epson says it won the Nikkei Award for Superior Products and Services in 1982. The 1984 edition of the Guinness Book of World Records recognised the device as the world's smallest television. As for sales, that was another story. The Smithsonian Insider reported that the product appeared in the U.S. market in 1983 for $500. Carlene Stephens, a watch curator at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History, says it did not really catch on. In her opinion, the watch itself was not that big, but people didn't like carrying the battery pack around. A gadget that needed a cable up a sleeve and a box in a pocket was a pretty hard sell.Today, more powerful screens sit in pockets and on wrists. Stephens says the wrist is a spot manufacturers find it hard to resist because it is personal, easy to use and always available. She also notes that the Apple Watch was not the first attempt to put the latest tech on the wrist, and she uses Seiko's TV watch as one of her examples. It was an attractive idea in itself, even if the equipment around it was pretty elaborate. But as a piece of design history, that tiny screen on the wrist can be a nice reminder of just how far portable tech has come.
Article Summary: Seiko's LCD TV watch, launched in 1982, had a 1.2-inch screen, but a cable ran up the sleeve to a separate receiver carried in a pocket. The watch could still perform basic tasks like the alarm, chronograph, calendar and also tune in to FM radio. Seiko Epson says the TV consumed less power than any before it and could run up to five hours on two AA batteries.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:
Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile (Photo: AP).

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.

Article Title: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora warns AI is making hacking ‘dangerously’ easy, explains how
Article Text:
Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks

Nikesh Arora: One hacker can now do the work of 19 using AI agents

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora has issued a stark warning that artificial intelligence (AI) is making cyberattacks significantly easier to execute, pointing out that AI tools are uncovering decades of human coding flaws at an alarming pace, and hackers are reaping the rewards. Speaking at an Economic Times event, Arora noted that Anthropic’s Mythos is rapidly exposing 50 years' worth of human software mistakes in a remarkably short timeframe, handing a major advantage to cybercriminals. He also highlighted that the flaws that were deemed ‘uncrackable’ by humans, are being exploited by criminals with the new technology.“We've written bad code for 50 years. And unfortunately, AI is busy finding out all those vulnerabilities in a very short span of time. And it's ended up being a bit of a boon for bad actors whose entire reason to exist is that they look for ways to get into companies,” Arora said.To illustrate just how much the threat landscape has shifted with AI, Arora pointed to a recent real-world incident showing how the technology multiplies a single attacker's reach. He said that in one recent case, a single hacker used an AI model on the dark web to attack 19 companies at the exact same time.According to Arora, an operation that previously would have required 19 people working over many days was carried out by one individual deploying an AI agent across all 19 targets.“So I think that is just the beginning. It is unfortunately most likely to come to a theater near you,” he noted, adding that beyond speeding up attacks, AI is breaking through security flaws that human experts once thought were safe from exploitation.“There have been vulnerabilities which were deemed to not be crackable by humans. AI has been able to crack those,” he explained, adding that the industry has entered a new era where organisations must go back and repair historical security flaws they created over the decades.“There have been vulnerabilities which were deemed to not be crackable by humans. AI has been able to crack those. So I think we're in a bit of a new era where we're going to have to go fix all these problems that we've created historically and that is going to be a journey. It's going to take us 12 to 18 months and I think it's going to be a bit of an open season for bad actors,” he said.
Article Summary: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora warns that artificial intelligence is making cyberattacks significantly easier to execute. Article Title: One of world’s most widely used password managers hacked, customer names and emails stolen: Read what the company has to say
Article Text:
1Password hacked : How the breach happened

What data was stolen and what stayed safe

Personal and account identifiers: Customer names, email addresses, account and user IDs, along with account creation and last sign-in timestamps.

Non-secret technical parameters: Public keys, which are public by design and pose no security risk,, Secure Remote Password protocol parameters, which cannot be used to log into an account, and internal architectural metadata such as numeric version and file identifiers.

Email link tokens: Tokens included in certain emailed links used for account recovery, SCIM Bridge, or Hosted Provisioning invitations.

Customer vaults and all stored items inside them

Encryption keys protecting user vaults

Account passwords and Secret Keys (which 1Password does not store or have access to)

Account recovery keys

1Password apps and browser extensions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Steps 1Password has taken and advice for users

Popular password manager 1Password has confirmed a security breach in which an attacker broke into some of its backend systems and stole limited account details, including names and email addresses, belonging to a subset of its users. The company stressed that despite the intrusion, the customer vault data, stored items, account passwords and secret keys remain completely safe and were never accessed. 1Password noted that its apps, browser extensions, and services continue to operate normally, and users do not need to make any changes to their accounts. The company has also explained how the hacking happened, and shared advice for users.According to 1Password, the incident began on November 19, when the company started investigating signs that an attacker had compromised an employee’s corporate GitHub account. Using that access, the intruder pulled source code from private repositories, gained entry to 1Password's CI/CD system, and pushed malicious code to backend services to download administrative customer records.It clarified that its source code holds no user secrets, and while the CI/CD system contains infrastructure-related secrets required for the product to run, the company has rotated all potentially exposed credentials with no impact on product security or service availability.For the affected subset of users, the downloaded records included:1Password explained that only a small number of users had active provisioning or recovery tokens during the breach, and those individuals have been notified directly. These tokens cannot grant account access as they only work alongside a Single Sign-On (SSO) login or a verification code sent to the user's registered email address, the company noted.Crucially, the company emphasised that the following remained untouched:Following the discovery, 1Password disabled the compromised employee GitHub account, revoked the stolen token and removed the unauthorised access. The company also rotated or revoked all potentially exposed internal credentials, tightened controls across GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoints, added new threat detections, and brought in independent cybersecurity experts to verify its containment and cleanup.To further protect against brute-force guessing, 1Password expanded the verification codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric characters. The company also confirmed it has found no internal evidence of any user account takeovers resulting from the exposed tokens.While users do not need to update their account settings, 1Password is urging everyone to stay alert for phishing attempts, such as unexpected emails, texts, or phone calls mentioning 1Password, account invitations, or recovery requests they did not initiate.
Article Summary: password manager 1Password confirms a security breach. An attacker broke into some of its backend systems and stole limited account details, including names and email addresses, belonging to a subset of its users. The company stressed that the customer vault data, stored items, account passwords and secret keys remain completely safe and never accessed.

Article Title: Claude users can now build their own Mac and Windows apps without writing code
Article Text:
Claude can now build your desktop apps

Anthropic keeps full computer access for apps users build themselves

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Claude desktop apps still need an internet connection and a Claude login

Anthropic is letting Claude users turn their artifacts into desktop apps for Mac and Windows. The "Install as app" feature is rolling out in beta on every Claude plan, including the free tier, with no coding, app packaging or API key needed.Once installed, a Claude artifact gets its own icon and window, and can be shared with others. On a Mac, these apps sit in a "Claude Apps" folder within Applications, so they show up in Spotlight and can be pinned to the Dock.To install one, users open an artifact in the Claude desktop app, head to the Share menu and pick "Install as app". The apps can still use Claude and any connected services, and they update automatically when the original artifact is edited. Every request an app sends to Claude counts toward the plan's usage limits."If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention," Anthropic said. Its staff have already built an image editor, a file manager, a folder organiser, a terminal and a performance monitor with it.Permissions come in three levels. By default, an installed app can only do what an artifact could do in a browser.It can then ask for app permissions such as sending notifications, adding a menu bar or system tray item, floating over other windows and responding to keyboard shortcuts.The top level is full computer access, which lets an app run programs and read, change or delete files without asking each time. Anthropic does not review apps before they are installed, so users can only grant this to apps they made themselves. On Team and Enterprise plans, that extends to apps built by colleagues.Permissions also reset with every update, including the user's own edits.Under the hood, these are web-based apps that run through the main Claude app, which has to be installed and signed in, with an internet connection, for them to open. The feature is not available on Linux, the web or mobile, or to organisations with HIPAA-ready setups.Artifacts made from templates such as Claude Docs, Slides and Sheets cannot be installed. If someone stops sharing an app, the programs it started stop within about 20 minutes.The feature is on by default for Team plans, with full computer access switched off. Enterprise plans keep it off until an owner turns it on.
Article Summary: Anthropic lets Claude users turn their artifacts into desktop apps for Mac and Windows. The feature is rolling out in beta on every Claude plan, including the free tier. Once installed, a Claude artifact gets its own icon and window, and can be shared with others.

Article Title: Black Friday shopping: 5 ways ChatGPT can help shoppers save money
Article Text:
Find the best deal, not just the biggest discount

Keep an eye on sold-out products

Look beyond five-star ratings

Decide whether an upgrade is actually worth it

Give your shopping cart a reality check

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Shop smarter, not just cheaper

Black Friday has evolved into much more than a single day of discounts. For shoppers, it now means navigating countless product listings, flash sales, limited-time offers, cashback deals and ever-changing prices across multiple platforms. While the promise of saving money attracts millions of buyers, the sheer volume of deals can make it difficult to determine whether a purchase is genuinely worthwhile. This year's sale season is also seeing artificial intelligence play a bigger role in helping consumers make purchasing decisions. OpenAI says ChatGPT can assist shoppers in comparing prices, analysing reviews, tracking inventory and even avoiding impulse purchases, turning the AI chatbot into a digital shopping companion.Here are five ways ChatGPT can help shoppers make the most of Black Friday deals.One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make during sale events is focusing solely on the percentage discount. A product advertised with a 40% discount may still cost more than the same item on another platform once additional offers are taken into account. ChatGPT can help compare prices across different e-commerce websites and official brand stores while factoring in bank discounts, coupon codes, cashback offers, exchange bonuses and delivery charges.Instead of looking at headline discounts, shoppers can use the AI tool to calculate the effective final price and identify which retailer is offering the best overall value.This can be particularly useful for expensive purchases such as smartphones, laptops and home appliances where even a small difference in pricing can translate into significant savings.Popular products often sell out within hours of a sale going live. Limited-edition sneakers, gaming consoles, beauty products and clothing in specific sizes are among the items that frequently disappear from digital shelves during major shopping events. OpenAI suggests using dot, ChatGPT's personalised AI agent, to monitor product availability and notify users when items are back in stock. Rather than manually checking websites throughout the day, shoppers can ask the AI to track a specific product and alert them if it becomes available below a specified price threshold.For consumers hoping to secure a hard-to-find product, this feature could save both time and frustration during the busy shopping season.A large discount and thousands of positive reviews can make almost any product look attractive. However, overall ratings often fail to reveal recurring issues that only emerge after extended use. ChatGPT can help shoppers analyse publicly available customer reviews from different platforms and identify common complaints, durability concerns and recurring problems. By focusing on long-term user experiences rather than promotional claims, shoppers can gain a better understanding of whether a product is truly worth buying.This approach can be especially useful when evaluating electronics, home appliances and other products where reliability matters more than first impressions.Black Friday sales often tempt consumers to spend more than they originally planned. Premium products can appear particularly attractive when their prices are reduced, even if a less expensive alternative would meet most needs just as well.ChatGPT can help by comparing products based on how shoppers intend to use them. Rather than focusing only on specifications, the AI can explain the practical differences between a premium product and a more affordable alternative.For example, shoppers considering expensive headphones, smartphones or laptops can ask ChatGPT to recommend lower-cost substitutes and explain exactly what features they would be sacrificing. This allows buyers to decide whether the upgrade offers genuine value or simply looks tempting because of the sale price.One of the biggest risks during Black Friday is overspending. Individual purchases may appear inexpensive, but multiple small transactions across several platforms can quickly exceed a budget. Before checking out, shoppers can share screenshots of their shopping carts with ChatGPT and ask the AI to evaluate their planned purchases. The chatbot can ask questions about existing products, expected usage and spending limits before categorising items into priorities such as "buy now", "worth considering" and "skip".This process can help distinguish genuine needs from impulse purchases driven by fear of missing out, ensuring that shoppers stay within budget while still taking advantage of worthwhile deals.Black Friday is often marketed as a race to secure the biggest discounts before they disappear. However, saving money is not always about finding the lowest price. It is also about avoiding unnecessary purchases and making informed decisions.By helping consumers compare deals, monitor stock levels, analyse reviews and evaluate purchases more critically, ChatGPT can act as a useful shopping assistant during one of the busiest retail periods of the year. For shoppers overwhelmed by endless discounts and promotional offers, a little help from AI could make the difference between a smart purchase and buyer's remorse.
Article Summary: ChatGPT can help shoppers compare prices, analyse reviews, track inventory and avoid impulse purchases. The chatbot can ask questions about existing products, expected usage and spending limits before categorising items into priorities. OpenAI suggests using dot, ChatGPT's personalised AI agent, to monitor product availability.

Article Title: Companies are setting up war rooms, flying to Seoul and searching eBay as AI drains the supply of memory chips
Article Text:
Representative Image. Credit: SK Hynix

The memory chip shortage is expected to last until at least 2028

Firms are flying to Seoul, taking loans and checking eBay for chips

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Hardware makers are raising prices again and again to keep up

Companies worldwide are scrambling for memory chips as artificial intelligence data centres soak up much of the global supply, The Wall Street Journal reports. Procurement teams are working out of war rooms, flying to South Korea to court chipmakers and scanning eBay for leftover stock. Some chip prices have risen as much as tenfold in the past year.Holiday shoppers are already paying for it. Apple has raised MacBook prices by $100 to $500 depending on the model, and the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max start $100 higher than last year. The Xbox now sells for $600, up 33% from a year ago, and Amazon's Echo Dot costs $80, a 60% jump. Motorola halved the storage on its latest Edge phone to 128GB and still raised the price by $50.Supply sits with three companies: Samsung and SK Hynix in South Korea, and Micron in the US. None of them can expand fast enough. Counterpoint Research expects DRAM capacity to grow 50% by 2028, when new factories come online. SK Hynix has sold out of DRAM and AI-focused high-bandwidth memory through 2029. Micron has presold at least $150 billion of supply.Handshake deals have given way to contracts of up to five years, with suppliers often asking for 25% to 30% upfront, Citi analyst Peter Lee told WSJ.Karma Automotive CEO Marques McCammon has flown to South Korea four times in six months.Taiwanese flash-drive maker Apacer has taken loans so it can pay the moment stock appears. Finland's Jolla calls a Shanghai agent every week and now stress-tests chips after finding used parts sold as new. At Purism, staff check eBay daily and buy lots as small as five units.Even Elon Musk got the runaround. A Capital Group fund manager recalled that Samsung chairman Lee Jae-yong reportedly brushed off Musk's offers of long-term commitments and factory financing, because every buyer was offering the same.Framework Computers now revises prices almost monthly, and some of its high-end desktops cost about 70% more. Australia's Blackmagic Design has raised the price of one live-production system three times since April, from about $120,000 to $175,000. Late last year, thieves also took flash memory worth around $100,000 from one of its Indonesian warehouses. "They're not memory chips, they're memory bullions," CEO Grant Petty told WSJ.A driver-assistance developer advised by Seraph, a Las Vegas consultancy, has paid up to 40 times its budgeted price for one component. It plans to raise its own prices next year.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul has signed a law banning the manufacture, distribution and sale of toys with built-in AI companion chatbots for five years. The law takes effect on February 22, 2027, and companies that violate it could face civil penalties of up to $15,000 a day for each violation.It applies to products designed or intended for children aged 12 and younger, including stuffed animals, dolls and robots that use AI companions to hold conversations. With the ban taking effect after the holiday shopping season, Hochul urged families buying gifts to check whether a toy can carry on open-ended conversations with a child and what information it collects.The law also prohibits businesses from exchanging covered toys or holding them for sale in the state. The attorney general can ask a court to stop an operator from continuing or proceeding with a prohibited activity. Once a court finds that a violation occurred, the state does not have to prove that anyone was injured.The Contixo AI Pixie Paw Interactive Plush Cat, marketed to children as young as three, described firing squads and massacres during NBC News testing. Amazon, Target, Walmart and Macy’s removed the plush cat from their listings after NBC News contacted retailers about the findings.Contixo also took the product off its own website.The U.S. Public Interest Research Group Education Fund found that two other toys, the Alilo Smart AI Bunny and the GoLabs AI Panda, gave sexually explicit responses. Amazon and Walmart removed both products, while Macy’s pulled the bunny, NBC News reported. Some toys also switched languages without being asked, and products marketed as spelling assistants misspelt common words.More than 155 child safety advocates and technology experts sent a letter to Amazon and eBay on Monday asking the companies to bar AI toys from their marketplaces. An eBay spokesperson told NBC News that the company regularly reviews its policies and works with regulators.California Governor Gavin Newsom signed a similar law in September. California’s four-year moratorium on toys with AI companion chatbots begins on January 1, 2027, and runs until January 1, 2031.New York also enacted a separate chatbot safety law in October. That measure restricts features that can encourage emotional dependence or engage minors in sexual conversations.

Article Title: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas says AI can predict the future with its new ‘Time Machine’
Article Text:
A ‘time machine’ for the web

How the Time Machine works

Why it matters for AI forecasting

Early tests show promising results

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pricing and limits

Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas has announced a new feature called Time Machine, describing it as a way to allow artificial intelligence models study the Internet as it existed in the past and become better at predicting future events. The feature is presently available via Perplexity’s Search and Context APIs. In a post shared on social media platform X, Srinivas wrote, “We're building a time machine for the internet. Perplexity Time Machine shows a model the web exactly as it was on any date you pick. This allows you to post-train agents that can be good at predicting the future. Live today in our Search and Context APIs.”According to Perplexity, the new tool allows developers to freeze the internet at a specific moment in time and provide AI models access only to information that existed on that date. The feature currently supports snapshots of the web going back up to 365 days.The idea behind the tool is to help train and evaluate AI systems without allowing them to access information that became available later. Perplexity argues that this creates a more realistic environment for testing whether an AI model can reason about future outcomes rather than simply searching for answers that are already knownDespite the headline-friendly name, Time Machine doesn’t forecast anything on its own.It is a way of freezing the web at a past moment. Each time Perplexity reads a page for its web index, it saves a copy with the time it was saved. Developers add one setting, a cutoff date, to a Search API or Context API request, and search then considers only pages that existed by that date. Leaving the setting out returns today’s web. The Context API returns the archived full text of a page without contacting the live site. At launch, the stored snapshots reach back up to 365 days.The practical problem is that AI agents trained or tested on predictions can accidentally see the answer. A model asked to forecast an event from last month could find articles about what happened. Perplexity says Time Machine stops an agent from looking up the answers it is meant to predict, and uses forecasting agents as its worked example. Developers can have an agent research the web as it stood on a past date, make a forecast, then score it against what actually happened, which gives them a way to train and evaluate forecasting agents.Perplexity said it tested Time Machine by training a model called GLM-5.3 Flash on resolved political prediction questions from Polymarket. According to the company, the model improved its score from 0.77 to 0.80 after training with Time Machine, slightly outperforming Polymarket's own market odds score of 0.79.The company also compared its offering with a competing service called Exa Snapshot and said Time Machine delivered publication dates for a significantly higher percentage of webpages while reducing instances where future information leaked into historical searches.Time Machine works with existing API keys and endpoints and carries no surcharge. Search costs $5 per 1,000 requests, and Context costs $1 per 1,000 URLs fetched. It works with the default web and fast search types and cannot be combined with the recency filter or date filters.
Article Summary: Time Machine is a way of freezing the web at a past moment. Perplexity said it tested Time Machine by training a model called GLM-5.3 Flash on resolved political prediction questions from Polymarket. According to the company, the model improved its score from 0.77 to 0.80 after training with Time Machine.

How Muse and Meta’s own AI chips fit into those plans

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang says he and CEO Mark Zuckerberg talk frequently about plans that run from day-to-day product decisions to investments that take years. Wang pointed to Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent, as an example of the decisions they make each week as the company rolls out features and expands into new countries.Speaking on The Eric Newcomer Show, Wang said the pace of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry means the two have to plan across three time scales. The immediate decisions are about what to launch and where. Over the following months, the focus is on what Meta’s AI researchers should work on and how that work is progressing. The multiyear plan covers computing infrastructure, from data centres to chips Meta designs itself.Asked about working with Zuckerberg, Wang said,Meta launched Muse in the UK on November 23, making it available to adults on iOS, Android, the web and WhatsApp. The agent runs on Muse Spark, the first model from Meta Superintelligence Labs. It can work across connected apps and websites to carry out tasks and asks for approval before taking actions such as sending an email or making a purchase.On the hardware side, MTIA stands for Meta Training and Inference Accelerator, the company’s family of custom AI chips. In March, Meta said it planned to develop and deploy four new generations of MTIA chips over two years to support workloads including recommendations and generative AI. The chips are one part of the longer-term computing plan Wang described, alongside the data centres that house them.

Article Title: Can you play as Jason and Lucia together in GTA 6? Character-switching explained
Article Text:
Rockstar Games

GTA 6 allows players to switch between Jason and Lucia during gameplay

Can two players control Jason and Lucia together in GTA 6?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Grand Theft Auto 6 gives players two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who share a story and work together as partners. But can players actually take control of both characters at the same time? The answer is yes and no. GTA 6 allows players to bring Jason and Lucia together for activities, missions and robberies, but they cannot directly control both characters simultaneously. Instead, the game uses a character-switching system that lets players take control of either protagonist whenever the story and gameplay allow it.GTA 6 features a dual-protagonist system that allows players to experience the story through Jason and Lucia. Players can switch between the two characters once the option becomes available in Chapter 2.On PlayStation 5, players can hold the right button on the D-pad and press R1 to switch characters. On Xbox Series X|S, the corresponding button is RB. This allows players to take control of either protagonist while exploring the open world.However, switching characters is not the only way to play as a pair. Players can also invite Jason or Lucia to join them during free-roam activities.The other character can accompany the player, drive a vehicle or provide support during certain situations.The system also allows players to split up when they want to explore separately. This gives them more freedom to decide how they want to approach activities across Leonida.Although Jason and Lucia can participate in activities together, GTA 6 does not offer a local split-screen or online co-op mode that allows two people to control the protagonists separately. It remains a single-player experience.Players can still take both characters on several activities, including robberies. For example, Jason can drive the getaway vehicle while Lucia handles the shooting. Players can also switch control between them during certain situations.However, the character-switching system has some restrictions. Certain missions require players to use a specific protagonist, while other missions allow them to switch freely. Some story sequences also force players to change characters at particular moments.Rockstar designed the system around the game's story, so players cannot switch between Jason and Lucia whenever they want.GTA 6 lets players bring Jason and Lucia together and control either character during gameplay. However, those looking for a two-player co-op experience will have to play separately, as the game does not support two people controlling the protagonists at once.
Article Summary: GTA 6 gives players two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who share a story and work together as partners. Players can switch between the two characters once the option becomes available in Chapter 2. The game does not offer a local split-screen or online co-op mode that allows two people to control the protagonists separately.

Jaguar on Friday unveiled the Type 01, an all-electric luxury car that marks a new beginning for the British carmaker. Revealed in New York City, the four-door grand tourer combines high performance with modern design and new technology. One of the car's biggest highlights is its acceleration. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque.The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It comes with a 118kWh usable battery pack and offers a claimed range of up to 400 miles under US EPA testing. Its range is up to 450 miles (720km) under WLTP testing.The car uses an 850-volt electrical system that supports fast charging. Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
